newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - March 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BEAR STEARNS SUSPENDS DEALER

A derivatives trader alleged to be responsible for mispricing options and causing a 50 million stg drop in NatWest Markets profits, was suspended by his new employers last night. Bear Stearns had lured the trader from NatWest last December, and suspended him yesterday after news that NatWest Markets had reported him to the Securities & Futures Authority.
-- HAYS READY TO GO SHOPPING WITH 200 MILLION STG

Hays, the logistics and business services group, is ready to make acquisitions and can increase borrowings by 200 million without having to issue new shares, according to corporate development director Graham Williams. Hays reported half year pre-tax profits rose from 60.8 million stg to 64.2 million stg.
-- MORE PRIZES FOR PREMIUM BOND HOLDERS

National Savings is to increase the number of monthly prizes in the Premium Bond draw from June after complaints from holders that they were not winning often enough. There is currently around 7.8 billion stg invested in Premium Bonds and more than 30 million stg paid out in prizes each month. The number of monthly prizes will increase from 350,000 to 430,000.
THE TIMES
-- CLARKE KEEN TO KEEP LID ON INTEREST RATES

The Chancellor, Kenneth Clarke, speaking at the annual dinner of the British Retail Consortium last night, gave an upbeat assessment of Britain's economic prospects. He suggested he would maintain his stance against putting up interest rates in the run up to the election.
-- ROCK WINDFALL TO TOP 1,300 STG

Customers of Northern Rock can expect a windfall of up to 1,475 stg following the society's stock market debut in October. The 900,000 saving and borrowing members will receive 500 shares, estimated to be worth between 260p and 295p. Northern Rock defended its decision to make a basic distribution of an equal amount of shares to members, saying eight out of ten members would be better off than under a variable benefit scheme.
-- FORWARD CHIEF'S FAMILY MAKES 50 MILLION POUNDS

The electronics company the Forward Group has accepted a 129 million stg takeover bid from PCB Investments of America. Chairman Raymond Chamberlain will make a personal profit of 15 million stg from the deal. PCB has so far only secured the Chamberlain family's 40 percent stake in Forward at 230p per share. If the takeover goes ahead, Mr Chamberlain's immediate family will a further 35 million stg.
THE GUARDIAN
-- AFTER NATWEST, BONUS CURBS

A new initiative to stamp out wild risk taking in the City by derivatives traders through revamping bonuses is expected to come about after the 50 million stg scandal at NatWest Markets. Futures and Options Association chief executive Anthony Bellchambers said his organisation was likely to consider proposals to provide better links between salaries and long term performance.
-- US RECRUITMENT RIVAL BUYS MICHAEL PAGE FOR 346 MILLION STG

Britain's biggest executive recruitment consultancy, Michael Page, has agreed to a 346 million stg bid from Interim Services, an American rival. The deal will create one of the biggest groups of its kind. Michael Page chairman Lord Wakeham said combining the two businesses was a logical step, with little duplication of activity and almost no job losses likely.
-- TOUGH BUDGETS AHEAD TO AVERT DELAY TO EMU

Yves Thibault de Silguy, the European commissioner responsible for the single currency has said European leaders are prepared to take further tough budgetary action to ensure their countries qualify for the single currency and avoid a delay which could put an end to the project.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- BBC PAY-TV DEAL WITH FLEXTECH CLOSE

The BBC is expected to sign its deal with Flextech to provide a pay TV service this week. It emerged yesterday that Flextech will put up 20 million stg for a 50 percent stake in the venture that will run for 30 years. The two sides are both optimistic that the new channels will be up and running on schedule this summer.
-- ROTHERMERE DESCENDANTS CASH IN WITH 160 MILLION STG DAILY
MAIL PLACING

Seven members of the Rothermere dynasty are to sell shares worth 169 million stg in the Daily Mail & General Trust. It will be one of the family's biggest transfers of ownership. The placing of 11 percent of the Daily Mail to Evening Standard newspaper empire's non-voting shares will not harm the Harmsworth family's grip on the company.
